The bug: my `regtok` regex `V([0-9A-F])` also matches the `VK`/`VF` pseudo-registers, so `LD VK, V4` falls into the wrong assembler branch. Isolating the fix:

The same failure means the `LD` dispatch itself is wrong — `LD VK, V4` has no Vx first operand, so it falls into the `LD F, addr` branch. Writing the correct dispatcher and testing end-to-end:

The `LD VK, V4` line has `VK` as the *first* operand — my dispatcher only checked `V[0-9A-E]` and `F` there, so it fell through. Adding the `u(0)=='K'` branch and running the full test suite (no-key soak + key-injected runs + screen renders):

Error: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/tmp/refio-import-XHHMj1/.refio_run_1793219818469.py", line 210, in <module> rom = asm(DEMO) ^^^^^^^^^ File "/tmp/refio-import-XHHMj1/.refio_run_1793219818469.py", line 64, in asm else: raise AsmError(f'bad LD at {pc:#05x}: {l}') ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^…
The `u(0)=='K'` check alone doesn't match `VK` — the token is literally `VK`. That's the real bug. Fixing it and running the full test suite:
